method: Independent exact normalized-Dicke splitting and full cross-reduction matrices; no builder functions imported. Every lower bound recomputed from exact subspaces only, each upper bound recomputed from Schmidt and tensor-Gram inequalities plus supplied pure-state exclusions, and all proof associations checked. The N=12,t=2 complement certificate is independently reconstructed with exact rational arithmetic. Spin-error saturation is also excluded whenever no integer tensor rank has the required Casimir eigenvalue. Every conjectured dimension is checked against Figure 2. The three new dimension-three examples are checked by their exact radical or rational-isolation verifiers; the exported symbolic coefficients and parameter definitions must match the certified basis exactly. The N=8 first- and second-order exclusions are rechecked exactly, including the auxiliary pure-state recoupling identities and the vectorization lift; its general even-N first-order consequence is applied only on the proved domain. The N=9 second-order exclusion is reconstructed with exact Young-symmetry contraction equations and a strictly positive diagonal identity.
limitations: Numerical basis checks remain approximate and do not establish exact existence or maximality.
The linked pure-state exclusion proofs are reused rather than reproved by this audit.
Individual Majorana coordinates are tested separately by reconstructing the vectors.

n18FourthOrderInertia.compressionArgument: Every first-spin operator in a degree-four polynomial in J.S has spin-tensor ranks at most 4. Its scalar coefficient is fixed by the partial trace over spin 9. That partial trace vanishes, so the polynomial contains only first-spin ranks 1..4. Every such tensor compresses to zero on an AC4 subspace. Hence C tensor V3 is a 7k-dimensional totally isotropic subspace. A nonsingular Hermitian form of inertia (13,120) admits no totally isotropic subspace larger than 13.
